To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
attentional deployment is a contributing factor to successful emotion regulation.

attentional deployment is different across emotion regulation strategies, and that successful emotion regulatory outcomes depend on the extent to what people look toward emotional information in complex visual scenes.

1) people who looked toward emotional content during emotion regulation reported less negative emotional experience; 2) expressive suppressers looked away from the emotional content of complex scenes during emotion regulation, and this effect was more pronounced for the suppressers than the reappraisers; 3) reappraisers looked away from emotional content more than the suppressers; and 4) the extent to which participants looked away from the emotion content of complex scenes did not predict emotional experience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of attention in emotion regulation.
the cognitive and perceptual processes that underlie emotion regulation and the implications for emotion dysregulation in psychopathology.
the cognitive processes that underlie successful emotion regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
attentional deployment plays an important role in the regulation of emotion.
attentional deployment plays a key role in the success of emotion regulation strategies, with implications for the understanding of the cognitive and neural mechanisms of emotion regulation.
attentional deployment is a key factor in the success of emotion regulation, and that it is important to look before you regulate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

attentional deployment is a critical factor for successful emotion regulation and that it may play an important role in the differential effects of cognitive reappraisal versus expressive suppression on emotion experience.
the deployment of attention during emotion regulation is a key factor that contributes to the divergent effects of cognitive reappraisal vs. expressive suppression on emotion regulation success.
attentional deployment may be an important component of successful emotion regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cognitive mechanisms underlying emotion regulation may be more complex than previously thought.
emotion regulation strategies may differentially affect attentional deployment to emotional areas of a visual scene.
the deployment of attention is an important factor to consider when studying the effects of emotion regulation strategies on emotional experience.
